items.title: Steve Buckingham, interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, February 25, 2019 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: And then on the other hand there’s anecdotes like Jimmy Cobb the drummer who played on “Kind of Blue?”

ctx.x: triple scale thinking it would cut back but they kept paying them and they were still working seven days making triple scale instead of double scale.
And then on the other hand there’s anecdotes like Jimmy Cobb the drummer who played on “Kind of Blue?” He made like less than a hundred bucks for that thing.

Well scale like I say is much different now. But again not that many people use studio players anymore. Like I say in Nashville the country records, it’s still mostly studio guys. I know they still put together jazz groups to play in the studio. But “Kind of Blue,” what year was that? Early 60s?
